subject: Archaeology
title: Pets of the Pharaohs
description: A quick win: understand Pets of the Pharaohs.

hook.text: Egyptians loved their pets so much that killing a cat — even accidentally — was punishable by death.

buildup.text: Cats were sacred to the goddess Bastet. Families shaved their eyebrows when a household cat died.

discovery.text: Millions of mummified cats, dogs, baboons, and even fish have been found in Egyptian animal cemeteries.

twist.text: Many animal mummies were bred and killed specifically for sale as religious offerings — a commercial industry.

climax.text: X-rays show some 'cat mummies' contain no cat at all — just sticks and rags. Ancient fraud existed too.

punchline.text: Even in ancient Egypt, people sold fake goods to the faithful.

quiz.question: What did X-rays reveal about some Egyptian animal mummies?
options: Many animals had been poisoned before mummification
Some contained no animal at all — just sticks and rags
They were far older than the surrounding human burials

details.summary: Ancient Egyptians kept cats, dogs, monkeys, gazelles, and even baboons as pets. Cats were particularly revered for their association with the goddess Bastet. Pet animals were often mummified and buried with their owners, reflecting genuine emotional bonds.
details.whyItMatters: Pet burials and mummified animals reveal the emotional lives of ancient people. They show that the human-animal bond is not a modern phenomenon but a deep-rooted aspect of human culture across millennia.
takeaways: Egyptians kept cats, dogs, monkeys, and gazelles as pets
Cats were sacred to goddess Bastet and specially revered
Mummified pets buried with owners show emotional bonds

faq.question: Why were cats so special in ancient Egypt?
faq.answer: Cats killed snakes and rats that threatened grain stores, making them economically valuable. Their association with Bastet, goddess of home and fertility, elevated them to sacred status. Killing a cat, even accidentally, was a crime punishable by death.

faq.question: Have archaeologists found individual pet burials?
faq.answer: Yes. Dogs have been found buried with collars and names inscribed on their coffins. Cats were mummified with elaborate care. Some tomb paintings show owners with named pets, and pet mummies were placed in their owners' tombs to accompany them to the afterlife.
